questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why British people work long hours
How Finland made its inactive population healthier
The best types of exercise for office workers
Why video games are bad for children
questions.why: Catherine says the topic is how one country has been very successful in dealing with a sedentary population.

questions.q: How does Dan describe his own lifestyle?
options: He sits down almost all day and never exercises
He has an active job but is lazy at home
He doesn't need to exercise because he walks to work
His job involves a lot of sitting, but he exercises
questions.why: Dan says his job is pretty sedentary, but he goes to the gym and plays football, so his life isn't.

questions.q: What was Finland like 40 years ago?
options: Perhaps the unhealthiest country in the West
One of the healthiest and most active countries in Europe
A country with no heart disease
A country where people exercised every day
questions.why: Catherine says 40 years ago Finland was perhaps the unhealthiest country in the Western world.

questions.q: By how much have deaths from heart disease fallen in Finland?
options: By 10%
By half
By 80%
By 90%
questions.why: Dan says death by heart disease in Finland has fallen by 80%.

questions.q: What has happened to life expectancy in Finland?
options: It has stayed the same
It has risen by 10 years
It has risen by 80 years
It has fallen slightly
questions.why: Dan says life expectancy has risen by 10 years.

questions.q: How should we understand John Laurenson's description of unhealthy people?
options: As an official government report
As a serious criticism of Finnish people
As advice from a doctor
As a joke that is not meant seriously
questions.why: Dan says the report is 'quite tongue-in-cheek', meant to be funny and not taken seriously.

questions.q: According to Laurenson, what will the 'stern lady with a clipboard' do?
options: Force you to go to the gym
Give you a fine
Make firm suggestions, but not drag you out
Take away your computer and games console for a while
questions.why: He says they'll make firm suggestions but won't actually drag you off your PlayStation or out of the pub.

questions.q: What else does the report say Finland does to improve health?
options: It encourages healthy habits from school age
It bans fast food
It closes pubs early
It pays people money to exercise regularly
questions.why: Dan says there is a lot of encouragement, even from school age, to eat well and exercise.
